items.title: Corte de apelaciones de EEUU confirma la inclusión de Anthropic en lista negra del Pentágono
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Una corte federal de apelaciones declinó bloquear el viernes una orden del Departamento de Defensa que incluía a Anthropic en una lista negra de contratos militares y consideraba a esta compañía de inteligencia artificial un riesgo para la seguridad nacional.
items.body:
Una corte federal de apelaciones declinó bloquear el viernes una orden del Departamento de Defensa que incluía a Anthropic en una lista negra de contratos militares y consideraba a esta compañía de inteligencia artificial un riesgo para la seguridad nacional.
La sentencia de la Corte de Apelaciones para el Circuito del Distrito de Columbia se dictó en el marco de una demanda interpuesta por Anthropic contra la decisión del Pentágono de calificarla como un riesgo para la cadena de suministro en materia de seguridad nacional.
La empresa indicó que esta decisión ha supuesto pérdidas por valor de miles de millones de dólares y ha dañado su reputación de cara a su esperada próxima salida a bolsa.
Anthropic declaró en un comunicado que, aunque discrepa respetuosamente de la decisión, sigue confiando en su postura y está barajando sus opciones, incluida una nueva revisión judicial.
El mes pasado, un juez federal de San Francisco anuló una designación paralela en virtud de otra ley, al considerar que el Gobierno había tomado represalias ilegales contra Anthropic por sus opiniones sobre la seguridad de la IA.

items.title: George Russell grabs 5th pole of season at Azerbaijan
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Mercedes' George Russell clinched his fifth Formula 1 pole of the season at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on Friday.
items.body:
Mercedes' George Russell clinched his fifth Formula 1 pole of the season at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on Friday.
The Brit roared through the Baku street circuit in a time of 1:42.526 in Q3, comfortably ahead of runner-up Charles Leclerc of Ferrari at 1:43.363. McLaren's Oscar Piastri was third, just 0.001 seconds behind Leclerc.
Russell will be looking for his third win of the season on Saturday after finishing second to Red Bull's Max Verstappen at last year's Azerbaijan GP.
Mercedes teammate and current F1 points leader Kimi Antonelli of Italy crashed out of Q1 and will start 16th.
Red Bull's Isack Hadjar returned from a wrist injury and qualified fourth in his first action since the Hungarian GP on July 26.
The remainder of the top 10, in order, are McLaren's Lando Norris, Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, Alpine's Pierre Gasly, Verstappen, Williams' Carlos Sainz and Alpine's Franco Colapinto.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Knicks' Jalen Brunson 'fully cleared' after wrist surgery
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson said he is "fully cleared" to return following offseason wrist surgery.
items.body:
New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson said he is "fully cleared" to return following offseason wrist surgery.
The All-Star point guard had a procedure on his left wrist in July after leading New York to its first title in 53 years.
Brunson, 30, confirmed his readiness during an appearance Thursday on his "Roommates Show" on YouTube.
"As you guys know, I had surgery this offseason, and I just wanted to tell you guys that I am fully cleared," he told the crowd during a live taping at Randall's Island Park in New York City.
The 2026 Finals MVP averaged a playoff-high 28.4 points in the Knicks' 16-3 playoff march to the championship.
Brunson averaged 26.0 points, 6.8 assists and 3.3 rebounds in 74 games (all starts) during the 2025-26 regular season.
The Knicks' preseason opener is Oct. 5 at Philadelphia. They open the regular season at home against the 76ers on Oct. 20.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Perplexity AI sued by startup for allegedly stealing 'wake word' technology
items.author: Blake Brittain
items.creator: Blake Brittain
items.summary: Startup DaVoice has sued Perplexity AI in California federal court for allegedly stealing trade secrets related to "wake word" technology for AI assistants.
items.body:
Startup DaVoice has sued Perplexity AI in California federal court for allegedly stealing trade secrets related to "wake word" technology for AI assistants.
The heavily redacted complaint , filed on Thursday, said that Perplexity stole DaVoice's secrets after the companies collaborated on unspecified technology "built with DaVoice’s proprietary source code, inference logic, network architecture, training approaches, training data, and know-how."
Spokespeople for the companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Friday.
DaVoice specializes in technology that allows devices to continuously listen for "wake words" to activate them.
The startup said that it has collaborated with companies including Volkswagen and internet-of-things company Samsara.
Perplexity is best known for its AI-powered search engine technology and Comet browser and AI assistant
The case is DaVoice v. Perplexity AI Inc, US District Court for the Northern District of California, No. 3:26-cv-10909.
For DaVoice: Davida Brook and Ian Crosby of Susman Godfrey
For Perplexity: attorney information not yet available

items.title: Iran will make no nuclear concessions, Iranian official says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Iran will show no flexibility over its nuclear program even if the United States accepts its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which calls for steps including the lifting of a US naval blockade on Iranian ports, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday.
items.body:
Iran will show no flexibility over its nuclear program even if the United States accepts its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which calls for steps including the lifting of a US naval blockade on Iranian ports, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday.
The official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the waterway would remain closed until “all of Iran’s conditions are met” by the United States.
Under [USN:L6N45H06Z TEXT:"Iran’s proposal"], Tehran has offered to reopen the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz. Within seven days, hostilities would end on all fronts, including Lebanon, the United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports, release Iran’s frozen funds and waive its oil sanctions, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Thursday.
The proposal follows a sharp escalation in Middle East tensions after seven months of war between Iran and the United States, with Iran-backed Houthi militias in Yemen launching missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Congo military plane crash kills 13, including three officers, official says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Thirteen people including three army officers were killed on Friday when a military plane crashed in Democratic Republic of Congo, an official said.
items.body:
Thirteen people including three army officers were killed on Friday when a military plane crashed in Democratic Republic of Congo, an official said.
The plane was travelling to the capital, Kinshasa, from the southwestern city of Kikwit when it experienced a technical problem and attempted to land in Kenge, in Kwango province, said Remy Saki Bokinda, the Kwango vice governor. "With no landing strip available in Kenge, the plane crashed into a residential plot," he said.
The passengers included General Likulia Bakumi, the army's auditor general, as well as a major, a captain and other military personnel and civilians, Bokinda said.
"All those on board died; 12 were burned beyond recognition, while the pilot's lifeless body was found outside the aircraft," he said.
Congo's aviation accident investigation authority is launching a probe of the crash, a government statement said.
Congo's army suffered significant setbacks last year at the hands of Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 rebels who seized large swathes of the east.

items.title: Argentina pode obter uma receita agrícola quase recorde em 2027, prevê bolsa
items.author: Kylie Madry
items.creator: Kylie Madry
items.summary: A Argentina poderia obter uma receita quase recorde com as exportações agrícolas no próximo ano, já que os preços elevados das safras, uma colheita excepcional e interrupções no abastecimento em regiões exportadoras concorrentes impulsionam os embarques de grãos e o influxo de moeda forte, informou a Bolsa de Comércio de Rosário em um relatório divulgado na sexta-feira.
items.body:
A Argentina poderia obter uma receita quase recorde com as exportações agrícolas no próximo ano, já que os preços elevados das safras, uma colheita excepcional e interrupções no abastecimento em regiões exportadoras concorrentes impulsionam os embarques de grãos e o influxo de moeda forte, informou a Bolsa de Comércio de Rosário em um relatório divulgado na sexta-feira.
O setor agrícola poderia gerar cerca de US$40 bilhões em receitas de exportação em 2027, o que seria o segundo maior total anual já registrado, ficando atrás apenas de 2022, de acordo com o relatório. Para 2026, a bolsa estima US$35,2 bilhões.
As exportações agrícolas são a principal fonte de moeda estrangeira da Argentina, fundamental para reabastecer as reservas do banco central, estabilizar o peso e sustentar as finanças públicas.
A bolsa projeta que a safra total de grãos da Argentina em 2026/27 será de 156 milhões de toneladas métricas, uma das maiores já registradas.
Os preços internacionais do milho, do trigo e da soja têm sido sustentados por riscos de abastecimento relacionados ao conflito no Mar Negro, onde a interrupção das exportações russas e ucranianas reduziu a disponibilidade, segundo o relatório.
Os agricultores argentinos se beneficiaram dessa interrupção, afirmou a bolsa em um relatório separado, com vendas de milho acima de 1 milhão de toneladas por semana durante quatro semanas consecutivas e os compromissos de exportação de trigo atingindo seu nível mais alto em cinco anos para esta época da safra.
A demanda da Ásia tem sido notável, com compradores como a Indonésia se voltando para as safras argentinas.
A bolsa também informou que a arrecadação com impostos de exportação de grãos e subprodutos poderia subir para US$5,48 bilhões em 2027, um aumento de 16% em relação a este ano, mesmo que as alíquotas tributárias devam diminuir.

items.title: Mpox case confirmed in northeastern Congolese city at center of Ebola outbreak
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A laboratory-confirmed case of mpox was identified in the northeastern Congolese city of Bunia, the director of a local hospital and two health officials said, raising concerns about a resurgence of the disease as the country battles its worst Ebola outbreak on record.
items.body:
A laboratory-confirmed case of mpox was identified in the northeastern Congolese city of Bunia, the director of a local hospital and two health officials said, raising concerns about a resurgence of the disease as the country battles its worst Ebola outbreak on record.
The epidemic caused by the [USN:L6N45H0P8 TEXT:"Ebola outbreak"] was declared on May 15 in Ituri province, where Bunia is located, and has infected 7,890 people and killed 3,799, according to government data published on Thursday.
Mpox is a viral disease that causes fever and skin lesions and spreads through close physical contact.
Congo declared an end to mpox as a national public health emergency in April after a three-year outbreak that resulted in more than 34,000 confirmed cases nationwide. Authorities cautioned at the time that the virus had not been eradicated and could resurge.
The latest case involves a 21-year-old woman who was admitted to hospital on Thursday with lesions across her body consistent with mpox, hospital director Davin Ambitapio Musungufu said. She tested positive on Friday, he and two health officials told Reuters.
A second woman, aged 32, has been identified as a suspected mpox case and is awaiting laboratory results, Musungufu said. She and the confirmed patient have been isolated and are being cared for by a dedicated medical team.
Investigations are underway to trace contacts and identify the source of infection, Musungufu said.
Dr. Adelard Lofungola, a health official who served as deputy incident manager for Congo's mpox response, said five suspected mpox cases in Bunia were currently under investigation.
Health officials have reported an increase in mpox cases in several parts of the country over the past month, he said.
Lofungola said the Ebola outbreak's impact on Congo's health system was complicating efforts to monitor other infections.
items.raw_description: A laboratory-confirmed case of mpox was identified in the northeastern Congolese city of Bunia, the director of a local hospital and two health officials said, raising concerns about a resurgence of the disease as the country battles its worst Ebola outbreak on record.

items.title: UK's Pinewood Technologies shareholders approve $721 million Ridgeview takeover
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Shareholders of British automotive software firm Pinewood Technologies on Friday approved a £545 million ($721.14 million) take-private deal by US private equity firm Ridgeview Partners.
items.body:
Shareholders of British automotive software firm Pinewood Technologies (PINE.L) on Friday approved a £545 million ($721.14 million) take-private deal by US private equity firm Ridgeview Partners.
At a shareholder meeting on Friday, 99.76% of votes cast were in support of the takeover.
Pinewood's board in August [USN:L4N44G0MH TEXT:"had recommended"] Ridgeview’s offer valuing the company at £4.48 per share in cash.
Pinewood is the latest London-listed technology company to attract private equity interest as buyout firms continue to target UK-listed businesses seen as [USN:L6N42Y0HI TEXT:"undervalued"].
The deal is expected to become effective on October 9.
Pinewood provides a cloud-based platform to help car dealerships and manufacturers manage everything from vehicle sales and customer relationships to repairs and accounting.
Pinewood had also attracted interest from Apax Partners [USN:L4N3Z91Q8 TEXT:"in"][USN:L4N3Z91Q8 TEXT:" January"], with an offer valuing it at 500 pence-per-share. But the private equity firm [USN:L4N3Z91QU TEXT:"withdrew"] its approach in February citing challenging market conditions.
Shares of Pinewood have gained about 24.16% year-to-date.
($1 = 0.7557 pounds)
items.raw_description: Shareholders of British automotive software firm Pinewood Technologies on Friday approved a £545 million ($721.14 million) take-private deal by US private equity firm Ridgeview Partners.

items.title: US refiner Phillips 66 is using AI to predict outages and boost processing, executive says
items.author: Arathy Somasekhar
items.creator: Arathy Somasekhar
items.summary: Phillips 66 is using artificial intelligence to predict outages within its refining systems, save on maintenance costs and increase crude processing, said Tandra Perkins, an executive vice president at the US refiner.
items.body:
Phillips 66 (PSX.N) is using artificial intelligence to predict outages within its refining systems, save on maintenance costs and increase crude processing, said Tandra Perkins, an executive vice president at the US refiner.
"I need my systems up more than they're down, being able to predict that obviously saves on maintenance costs," Perkins said on Friday while speaking at the Reuters Momentum AI conference in Austin, Texas.
The increased availability allows for more crude to be processed by the refiner and capture more margins, Perkins said, without providing a number on cost savings.
The Houston-headquartered company, which has about 10 refineries, has been focused on operational cost savings, particularly on the refining side.

items.title: India's Zee escalates copyright fight against Reliance-Disney's JioStar
items.author: Arpan Chaturvedi
items.creator: Arpan Chaturvedi
items.summary: India's Zee Entertainment has asked the Delhi High Court to initiate contempt proceedings against Reliance-Disney joint venture JioStar, alleging it continued to use copyrighted content despite a court injunction, a legal filing shows.
items.body:
India's Zee Entertainment has asked the Delhi High Court to initiate contempt proceedings against Reliance-Disney joint venture JioStar, alleging it continued to use copyrighted content [USN:L4N41J12I TEXT:"despite a court injunction"], a legal filing shows.
The filing, dated September 21, escalates an ongoing copyright dispute between the companies. Zee alleges JioStar is guilty of "wilful disobedience" because it continued using Zee's music and songs in programmes broadcast on its platforms despite a court order barring such use.
JioStar, formed from the $8.5 billion merger of Reliance and Disney's Indian media assets in 2024, declined to comment. Zee did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
The copyright case was heard on Friday. A source aware of the details of Friday's court hearing told Reuters the Delhi High Court asked JioStar for a response to Zee's latest allegations and the case will be heard next in December.
The lawsuit began in April when Zee sought $3 million in damages, citing 50 alleged copyright violations involving content from its music division.
In May, the Delhi High Court ordered JioStar not to "use, publish, broadcast, stream, upload" any of Zee's licensed works.
JioStar's lawyers have previously told the court the alleged infringements were "unintentional" and "purely residual in nature". The company said in May that it had removed a substantial volume of Zee content following the expiry of licensing agreements.
In its latest filing, Zee cited six instances between May and July that it said showed the continued use of its copyrighted works by JioStar.
JioStar is "illegally and actively exploiting" the works, Zee said in the filing.
The case is one of several copyright disputes highlighting increasing competition over content rights as India's streaming and broadcasting market consolidates.
JioStar, backed by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, is India's largest media and entertainment company. Zee, one of India's oldest broadcasters, is a smaller rival.
The Disney-Reliance joint venture has also previously [USN:L4N41R1DU TEXT:"launched"] a legal battle against Zee, alleging the unauthorised broadcast of popular Bollywood movies at a time when JioStar held the rights to the content.

items.summary: San Francisco 49ers pass rusher Nick Bosa will be sidelined for a "few weeks" with a calf injury, ESPN reported on Friday.
items.body:
San Francisco 49ers pass rusher Nick Bosa will be sidelined for a "few weeks" with a calf injury, ESPN reported on Friday.
The five-time Pro Bowler sustained the injury during practice Thursday and could land on injured reserve, per the report.
Bosa is not expected to play on Sunday when the 49ers (2-0) host the Arizona Cardinals (1-1) in Santa Clara, Calif.
Bosa, 28, played a total of 70 snaps in the first two games while coming back from a torn right ACL sustained in Week 3 last season. He has recorded seven tackles (two for loss) with one quarterback hit.
Bosa has recorded 64.5 sacks, 13 forced fumbles, 169 QB hits and 285 tackles in 87 games (85 starts) since being drafted with the No. 2 overall pick by San Francisco in 2019.
--Field Level Media

CAIRO: Saudi , Turkish and Pakistani military chiefs are to discuss help for Saudi Arabia as it faces attacks by Yemen's Houthis , while Iraq further curtailed Iranian flights on Friday (Sep 25), in line with US pressure, and an Iranian official threatened retaliation.
The Houthis have launched strikes on the Saudi -backed government in Yemen and repeatedly fired into Saudi Arabia , disrupting oil flows from the world's largest energy exporter, as part of a wider Middle East war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb 28.
The military escalation continued this week despite a push during the UN General Assembly in New York to revive diplomacy to end the conflict, which quickly spread to Lebanon and the Gulf in March before escalating in Yemen in recent weeks.
With talks stalled and during a lull in direct fire by the US and Iran, Washington had shifted tactics to extend financial sanctions by targeting companies from third countries that do business with Iranian firms through "secondary sanctions".

Iranian airlines were barred from neighbouring countries including the Unite d Arab Emirates and Oman on Thursday in response to new US sanctions , the first big impact of the shift.
On Friday, the three other Iraqi airports that operate flights to and from Iran joined Baghdad airport in suspending them, sources and state media said.
A flight ban, if sustained, could deepen Iran's isolation and worsen an economic crisis in the country, which is already facing a US blockade of its seaports.
Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iran's supreme leader, accused regional countries of "alignment with America" for blocking flights .
"If Iran does not have the possibility to fly and receive airport services, then no country in the region will have this possibility either", he said in a social media post.

OIL EXPORTS SQUEEZED The war, which US President Donald Trump launched alongside Israel, has killed thousands of people and disrupted global trade and energy supplies, adding to inflationary pressures.
While the fighting between the US and Iran has been stop-start, Iranian allies have mobilised, with Hezbollah attacks triggering an Israeli invasion of Lebanon and the Houthi advance in Yemen prompting a new humanitarian crisis.
Iran and its allies have significantly squeezed oil exports from Saudi Arabia , a US ally. The Houthis have disrupted ship traffic at the mouth of the Red Sea, while Iran has limited tanker traffic at the Strait of Hormuz, the conduit for 20% of the world's oil exports before the war.
On Thursday, the Houthis said they had fired dozens of missiles and drones at Saudi targets, while Saudi authorities said they had intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Houthi fighters.
Later, Saudi Arabia 's Grand Mufti, the kingdom's top religious authority, called on soldiers to be ready to lay down their lives to fight the Houthis until the group was ousted from power.
Amid the fighting, the Saudi , Pakistani and Turkish foreign ministers met on Thursday for discussions under a defence pact signed in August .
They condemned attacks targeting the holy Saudi city of Mecca and other civilian sites, while affirming Saudi Arabia 's right to defend itself and planning a meeting between chiefs of staff on ways to assist the kingdom.
Turkey's defence ministry said Chief of General Staff General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu was travelling to Saudi Arabia on Friday to meet his Saudi and Pakistani counterparts.
Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan said the defence pact, which stipulates that an attack against one country be considered an attack against all, could lead to intelligence, logistical or ammunition support.
" More advanced military support could also be considered depending on the scale of the threat," Erdogan said in written responses to Newsweek.
The speaker of Turkey's parliament, which has yet to ratify the pact, said it could be expanded into a broader alliance "for the Muslim world" , including Iran.

Related:

SHUTTLE DIPLOMACY IN NEW YORK In New York, Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told reporters on Thursday that Tehran had conveyed a proposal to the US via intermediaries under which the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened if Tehran’s conditions were met.
Under Iran’s proposal, hostilities would end on all fronts, including Lebanon, within seven days. The US would lift its blockade on Iranian ports, release Iran’s frozen funds and waive its oil sanctions, he said.
"The Strait of Hormuz will be reopened on the last day," Araqchi said, adding that talks with the US on other issues, including Iran’s nuclear issue, would then start.
A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday that Tehran was reviewing Washington's response to its peace proposals.
Oil prices fell on Friday as markets weighed the possibility of a truce, despite the number of ships recorded transiting the Strait of Hormuz dropping to nine on Thursday, half the 10-day average.

items.title: Syracuse gains commitment of 5-star F Moussa Kamissoko
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: New Syracuse coach Gerry McNamara received a commitment Friday from Class of 2027 forward Moussa Kamissoko, just the second five-star recruit for the Orange in the past decade.
items.body:
New Syracuse coach Gerry McNamara received a commitment Friday from Class of 2027 forward Moussa Kamissoko, just the second five-star recruit for the Orange in the past decade.
The 6-foot-7, 180-pound Kamissoko attends SPIRE Academy in Geneva, Ohio. The 247Sports composite lists him as the No. 5 small forward and the No. 14 overall player in the nation in the class. He played last season at Long Island Lutheran.
The competition had been fierce for Kamissoko. He already took official visits to Illinois, BYU, Florida State, Virginia and Oklahoma State. Programs such as Alabama, NC State, Penn State and Providence also were trying to get his commitment.
A scheduled visit to UConn on Friday presumably was canceled. He also had visits to Baylor and Louisville arranged for next month.
Kamissoko is the first five-star prospect to pick the Orange since forward Donnie Freeman in 2024, per ESPN.
He is the second player to commit to Syracuse in the 2027 recruiting cycle, joining Jack Donohue, a 6-8 forward from The Newman School in Boston.
McNamara led Siena to a near-upset of No. 1 overall seed Duke in the first round of the NCAA Tournament last March. His name began swirling immediately when Syracuse fired Adrian Autry at the end of the season. Between his Siena success and his status as a program icon -- McNamara shared the court with fellow freshman Carmelo Anthony on the 2022-23 NCAA championship team -- he became the choice for the Orange.
McNamara is being tasked with returning Syracuse basketball to national prominence. A team that seemed to be a virtual lock for the tournament each season hasn't been there since 2021.
Syracuse finished last season with a 15-17 record (6-12 Atlantic Coast Conference).
--Field Level Media

items.title: 米軍が拿捕したイラン系大型タンカー、ゆっくりと米国に向けて航海中
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米海軍がイラン戦争初期に拿捕したイラン系スーパータンカー（超大型石油タンカー）2隻が、数週間後にも米国に到着する見通しだ。米当局は船舶と、積載する数億ドル相当の原油を差し押さえる方針。イラン産原油は米国への輸入が数十年にわたり禁止されており今回の航海は異例だ。

トランプ米大統領がイランに終戦を迫るため海上封鎖を実施した4月、大型タンカー「ティファニ」と「マジェスティックX」はインド洋で米軍に拿捕された。ブルームバーグがまとめた船舶データによると、両船はこの1週間、ブラジル沿岸を航行している。拿捕された3隻目の船も喜望峰を回り、大西洋を西へ向かっていることが確認された。

米司法省は4月、ティファニとマジェスティックXの没収手続きを開始した。国土安全保障捜査局はその後、タンカー本体と、積載していた約400万バレルのイラン産原油を差し押さえるため、令状を執行していると明らかにした。3隻目のタンカー「レノア（別名ダビナ）」は6月に拿捕された。

これらのスーパータンカーはそれぞれ200万バレルを輸送でき、積み荷全体の価値は現在の市場価格で約6億ドル（約950億円）に上る。いずれも通常の12～13ノットを下回る8～9ノット程度の速度で航行している。

イラン産原油が米国の港に到着すれば、2023年に没収された貨物が運ばれて以来となる。トランプ政権は過去のタンカー拿捕で、差し押さえた船舶と原油を売却して利益を得ようとしてきた。

ただ、こうした取り組みは過去に問題にも直面している。ベネズエラ封鎖中に拿捕した180万バレルの原油を積むタンカー「スキッパー」の場合、米政府による没収申し立てに船主は抵抗し、売却の阻止に動いた。トランプ政権がこのタンカーの維持に費やしたコストは4700万ドルに膨らみ、老朽化したタンカー本体の価値の約5倍に達した。

米司法省はその後、イランの石油タンカーを戦利品として拿捕する手続きを効率化・簡素化するため、長らく休眠状態にある海事戦時裁判所を復活させる準備を進めている。

items.title: Las sanciones de Trump están obstaculizando la reforma económica de Cuba, según viceministro
items.author: Jim Wyss
items.summary: El viceministro de Relaciones Exteriores, Carlos Fernández de Cossío, afirmó que una menor presión de Washington permitiría avanzar en las transformaciones económicas de la isla.
items.body: Bloomberg — Uno de los principales diplomáticos cubanos advirtió que las sanciones del presidente estadounidense Donald Trump están frenando los esfuerzos de la isla por reformar su economía y adoptar reformas capitalistas. “Si Estados Unidos reduce la presión, esas transformaciones en Cuba pueden avanzar mucho y volverse verdaderamente irreversibles, que es nuestro objetivo y, en teoría, lo que Estados Unidos quiere que suceda”, dijo el viceministro de Relaciones Exteriores, Carlos Fernández de Cossío, al presentador de Bloomberg This Weekend, David Gura. La administración Trump está castigando duramente a Cuba con sanciones económicas y un bloqueo de combustible de facto que han exacerbado los apagones y provocado escasez de productos básicos. Incluso cuando la red eléctrica funciona, las restricciones de combustible implican que la mayoría de la gente solo tiene electricidad durante unas pocas horas al día, afirmó De Cossío. Ver más: Trump califica a Cuba como un “Estado fallido” que “caerá”; Díaz-Canel le responde En respuesta a la crisis, Cuba ha presentado más de 170 propuestas, otorgando mayor libertad al sector privado y flexibilizando las normas sobre importaciones. Sin embargo, estas reformas de libre mercado no funcionarán, ya que Estados Unidos está “sometiendo al pueblo cubano a la opresión y la asfixia”, declaró el ministro encargado de gestionar las relaciones con Estados Unidos. Las conversaciones entre Washington y La Habana se han estancado prácticamente por completo debido a la continua presión estadounidense, añadió De Cossío. Asimismo, señaló lo que describió como contradicciones en el discurso de Trump ante las Naciones Unidas esta semana. “Dijo que Cuba es un Estado totalmente fallido, pero en la misma frase afirma que Estados Unidos está ejerciendo más presión que nunca. Es decir, reconoce que la presión estadounidense es la causa del fracaso”, declaró De Cossío. “Es como agredir a una víctima y luego culparla de su situación”. Poner fin a más de 67 años de gobierno de partido único en Cuba es una prioridad para Trump y el Partido Republicano. Sin embargo, algunos analistas sostienen que esto podría cambiar si los demócratas obtienen el control de la Cámara de Representantes y el Senado en las elecciones de mitad de mandato de noviembre. Ver más: Cuba admite que las 176 medidas económicas son un incierto: “No sabemos cuál será el resultado” Si bien De Cossío reconoció que los cubanos esperan que un cambio político en Washington alivie la presión sobre la isla, calificó esa opinión de “ilusión”. “No podemos quedarnos de brazos cruzados”, dijo. “Queremos llegar a una solución con Estados Unidos lo antes posible. Y lo que suceda internamente en Estados Unidos no tendrá una repercusión real en Cuba”. Al ser consultado sobre el aumento de los envíos de carga estadounidenses al incipiente sector privado cubano a pesar de las sanciones de Trump, De Cossío afirmó que su gobierno acoge con beneplácito el flujo de mercancías, aunque este no logre satisfacer la creciente demanda en la isla. “Es evidente que Estados Unidos busca generar una situación de dependencia”, declaró. “No queremos ser dominados por ningún otro país”. La situación geopolítica de Cuba dio un giro dramático en enero, cuando comandos estadounidenses capturaron al principal aliado de la isla, el presidente venezolano Nicolás Maduro, y lo trasladaron a Nueva York para ser juzgado por cargos de narcotráfico. Ver más: EE.UU. amplía sanciones contra Cuba y alcanza a una empresa de combustible y a un nieto de Raúl Castro Desde entonces, Venezuela ha cortado las exportaciones de combustible a Cuba y la presidenta interina Delcy Rodríguez ha recibido el apoyo de Trump, con quien se reunió esta semana al margen de la Asamblea General de la ONU. Líderes mundiales se reúnen en la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas. Delcy Rodríguez interviene en la Asamblea General de la ONU en Nueva York, el 23 de septiembre. Al preguntársele si Cuba todavía considera a Venezuela un aliado, De Cossío respondió que, si bien era un país “amigo”, “aliado es una palabra demasiado fuerte”. Ver más: Cuba afirma que diálogo con EE.UU. está paralizado mientras la isla enfrenta una “guerra sin bombas” También rechazó la idea de que Cuba pudiera ceder su riqueza mineral a Estados Unidos, como Venezuela lo ha hecho con su industria petrolera. “Los recursos de Cuba pertenecen al pueblo cubano”, afirmó. “Nuestro gobierno no tiene derecho a privarlos de ellos y entregárselos a otro país”. El viceministro de Relaciones Exteriores de Cuba restó importancia a la idea de que cualquier presión económica pudiera provocar el colapso del gobierno. En cambio, afirmó que es necesario llegar a un acuerdo en la mesa de negociaciones. “Agradeceríamos una solución”, dijo De Cossío, prediciendo que un acuerdo podría estar “lejos de lo que queremos, pero menos de lo que algunas personas en Estados Unidos podrían esperar”. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: Swedish police launch probe into possible election fraud around Stockholm
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Police said on Friday they had started preliminary investigations into five complaints of election fraud around Sweden's capital, days after a probe in another area, casting a further shadow over the September 13 national vote.
items.body:
Police said on Friday they had started preliminary investigations into five complaints of election fraud around Sweden's capital, days after a probe in another area, casting a further shadow over the September 13 [USN:L8N4590Y1 TEXT:"national vote"].
Sweden's [USN:L1N455016 TEXT:"parliamentary election"] saw the opposition narrowly defeat the incumbent right-wing government in a vote widely seen as a referendum on whether the far-right [USN:L1N40K0GO TEXT:"Sweden Democrats"] should be part of the next administration.
Stockholm police said they had started the preliminary investigations after receiving five complaints, including one about the vote in the suburb of Jarva.
Two of the cases also involved complaints of potential vote-buying, a police spokesperson added, declining to go into more detail or name the other areas.
It was not immediately clear what impact those cases might have on the result of the election in those areas if any wrongdoing was found.
On Tuesday, prosecutors said they were looking into potential fraud [USN:L1N45E0HN TEXT:"in the central Swedish town of Borlange"], a case that could put 11 parliamentary seats in play if the Election Review Board decides to order a re-run.
In a statement on Thursday, the Prosecution Authority said no indictments had been issued in relation to the allegations of fraud in Borlange and no suspects had been formally identified.
In that case, the investigation centres on the election of Mohamed Abdukardir Ali, a Left Party candidate for parliament, who unexpectedly overtook other representatives on the ballot for the party.
The Left Party said on Tuesday Ali would take a leave of absence while the allegations were being investigated. Reuters was not immediately able to reach Ali for comment.
Sweden's Election Review Board on Friday was not immediately available to respond to requests for comment on the new investigations.

items.title: Palmer misses too many England camps, says Tuchel
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: England coach Thomas Tuchel said forward Cole Palmer had missed another chance to impress after withdrawing from the squad ahead of Saturday's Nations League opener against Spain with injury.
items.body:
England coach Thomas Tuchel said forward Cole Palmer had missed another chance to impress after withdrawing from the squad ahead of Saturday's Nations League opener against Spain with injury.
The Chelsea player, who was left out of England's World Cup squad earlier this year after an injury-hit campaign affected his form, returned to Tuchel's plans following a strong start to the season.
Palmer has scored four goals and provided two assists in seven appearances for Chelsea so far, earning a recall for Nations League fixtures against Spain, the Czech Republic and Croatia. However, the 24-year-old was forced to pull out of the squad with a muscle problem.
"It's another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities," Tuchel told reporters.
"I don't blame him for it, it's just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries.
"I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team. For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity."
Tuchel rejected suggestions they were managing the player's workload by letting him leave camp.
The Chelsea attacker played the full 90 minutes in his side's defeat by Brentford before reporting for international duty.
"He plays with discomfort and pain and cannot play on the highest level with discomfort and pain," Tuchel said.
"Chelsea informed us. That is my understanding. We're not managing load.
"This is not an international break. It's a competitive environment where the players love to train and be together. That's what we created. We will never compromise on that.
"We will never let this feeling creep in that the players don't want to come. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England."
The three-week international window is the first under FIFA's revised match calendar, which combines the traditional September and October breaks.
England begin their Nations League campaign against world champions Spain at Wembley on Saturday before travelling to Prague to face the Czech Republic on September 29.
Tuchel's side then take on Croatia in Rijeka on October 3 before hosting the Czechs at Wembley three nights later in Group A3.

"I don't blame him for it, it's just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries.
"I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team. For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity."
Tuchel rejected suggestions they were managing the player's workload by letting him leave camp. 
The Chelsea attacker played the full 90 minutes in his side's defeat by Brentford before reporting for international duty.
"He plays with discomfort and pain and cannot play on the highest level with discomfort and pain," Tuchel said.
"Chelsea informed us. That is my understanding. We're not managing load.
"This is not an international break. It's a competitive environment where the players love to train and be together. That's what we created. We will never compromise on that.
"We will never let this feeling creep in that the players don't want to come. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England."
The three-week international window is the first under FIFA's revised match calendar, which combines the traditional September and October breaks.
England begin their Nations League campaign against world champions Spain at Wembley on Saturday before travelling to Prague to face the Czech Republic on September 29.
Tuchel's side then take on Croatia in Rijeka on October 3 before hosting the Czechs at Wembley three nights later in Group A3.

items.title: Allemagne AfD et CDU unis pour interdire à Heidenau la pose de plaques commémoratives de l'Holocauste
items.author: Emanuele Berro, Friederike Heine
items.creator: Emanuele Berro, Friederike Heine
items.summary: La ville d'Heidenau, dans l'est de l'Allemagne, a approuvé une motion du parti d'extrême droite Alternative pour l'Allemagne (AfD) et de l'Union chrétienne-démocrate (CDU) interdisant la future pose au sol de plaques commémoratives des victimes de l'Holocauste.
items.body:
La ville d'Heidenau, dans l'est de l'Allemagne, a approuvé une motion du parti d'extrême droite Alternative pour l'Allemagne (AfD) et de l'Union chrétienne-démocrate (CDU) interdisant la future pose au sol de plaques commémoratives des victimes de l'Holocauste.
Les "Stolpersteine" (littéralement "pierres sur lesquelles on trébuche") sont des pavés mémoriels créés dans les années 90 par l'artiste berlinois Gunter Demnig en hommage aux victimes du nazisme. On en trouve dans plusieurs villes d'Allemagne mais aussi dans d'autres pays européens.
La décision prise jeudi à Heidenau, une ville située près de Dresde, dans le Land de Saxe, intervient alors que l’AfD devance la CDU du chancelier au pouvoir Friedrich Merz dans les sondages nationaux après des succès régionaux.
L’AfD a souvent remis en cause la mémoire de l’Holocauste en Allemagne. Le cofondateur du parti, Alexander Gauland, a notamment qualifié l’époque nazie de simple "fiente d’oiseau" dans l'Histoire allemande.
Le conseil municipal de Heidenau a décidé que les futures commémorations se concentreraient sur un site situé dans le cimetière nord de la ville.
Cette décision a relancé le débat sur le respect par la CDU du "Brandmauer", un principe de "mur coupe-feu" informel selon lequel les principaux partis allemands excluent toute coopération officielle avec l’AfD.
Les sections locales de l’AfD et de la CDU n’ont pas répondu aux demandes de commentaires de Reuters dans l'immédiat.
"Je suis consternée qu’un parti démocratique ait choisi de soutenir une manœuvre aussi transparente de la part de l’AfD extrémiste", a déploré Charlotte Knobloch, présidente d’une association juive de Bavière, au groupe de presse Funke.
L’adoption de la motion allait à l’encontre d’une recommandation de l’administration municipale.
"Une interdiction générale des futurs Stolpersteine n’est ni nécessaire à la création d’un mémorial central, ni justifiée par la proposition elle-même", avait déclaré l’administration municipale dans un communiqué avant la décision.
Les partisans de la motion ont fait valoir que de nombreux habitants considéraient les "Stolpersteine" comme inappropriés car les passants peuvent marcher dessus.

items.title: Os maiores ataques e roubos no mundo das criptomoedas
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A corretora de criptomoedas Bitget afirmou nesta sexta-feira que criptomoedas no valor aproximado de US$350 milhões foram roubadas da plataforma.
items.body:
A corretora de criptomoedas Bitget afirmou nesta sexta-feira que criptomoedas no valor aproximado de US$350 milhões foram roubadas da plataforma.
No ano passado, invasores roubaram US$2,9 bilhões em criptomoedas em quase 150 ataques diferentes, segundo pesquisadores da TRM Labs.
Autoridades alertaram em julho que grupos do crime organizado utilizam criptomoedas para transferir fundos rapidamente entre países, sem recorrer ao sistema financeiro convencional.
Aqui estão alguns dos maiores roubos desde que o bitcoin surgiu, em 2008.
BYBIT Um valor recorde de US$1,5 bilhão em criptomoedas ether foi roubado da corretora Bybit em fevereiro de 2025, no que os pesquisadores consideraram o maior roubo de moedas digitais até o momento.
A polícia federal dos Estados Unidos (FBI) afirmou que a Coreia do Norte foi a responsável e que os fundos foram rapidamente convertidos em outras criptomoedas e, em seguida, dispersos por milhares de endereços em várias blockchains.
A Coreia do Norte negou ter organizado roubos de criptomoedas.
POLY NETWORK Hackers roubaram da Poly Network, uma plataforma que facilita transações de tokens ponto a ponto, cerca de US$610 milhões em agosto de 2021. Os hackers responsáveis pelo roubo devolveram posteriormente quase todos os recursos roubados.
RONIN NETWORK Em março de 2022, hackers roubaram criptomoedas no valor de cerca de US$540 milhões na época de um projeto de blockchain vinculado ao popular jogo online Axie Infinity.
A Ronin, uma rede que permite a transferência de criptomoedas entre diferentes blockchains, informou que os hackers roubaram cerca de 173.600 tokens de ether e 25,5 milhões de tokens de USD Coin.
COINCHECK Em janeiro de 2018, hackers roubaram da corretora Coincheck, com sede em Tóquio, cerca de US$530 milhões em criptomoedas, segundo valores da época . Os ladrões atacaram uma das “hot wallets” da Coincheck, uma carteira digital armazenada online, para drenar os fundos.
A agência de inteligência da Coreia do Sul afirmou na época que um grupo de hackers norte-coreano poderia estar por trás do roubo.
MT. GOX Em um dos primeiros e mais notórios ataques envolvendo criptomoedas, bitcoins no valor de quase US$500 milhões foram roubados da corretora Mt.Gox, em Tóquio, na época a maior do mundo, entre 2011 e 2014.
A Mt.Gox, que já havia movimentado 80% do comércio mundial de bitcoins, entrou com pedido de recuperação judicial no início de 2014 após a revelação do ataque, fazendo com que cerca de 24 mil clientes perdessem o acesso aos seus recursos.
(Por Tommy Reggiori Wilkes e Tom Wilson)

items.title: Cuántos salarios se necesitan para comprar un metro cuadrado en Buenos Aires
items.author: Redacción Bloomberg Línea
items.summary: La cantidad de salarios necesarios para ese fin trepó en julio respecto del mes previo, pero se mantienen por debajo de los requeridos hace un año y cuando Javier Milei asumió la Presidencia ...
items.body: Buenos Aires — Para comprar un metro cuadrado de un departamento en la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires se necesitan entre 2,8 y 3,5 salarios. Así lo reflejó un reciente informe del Instituto de Economía (INECO) de la Universidad Argentina de la Empresa (UADE), que calculó que la cantidad de salarios necesarios para ese fin trepó en julio respecto del mes previo, pero se mantienen por debajo de los requeridos hace un año y cuando Javier Milei asumió la Presidencia, en diciembre de 2023. Con respecto al mes anterior, el Índice de Salario Real en función del valor del M2 (ISRV) disminuyó en julio 3,3% para los inmuebles nuevos y 5,4% para los usados debido a la caída de los salarios en dólares y al aumento del valor del M2. En términos interanuales, el ISRV muestra un aumento del 7,2% para los departamentos nuevos y un 14,8% en los usados. Una caída de este índice refleja que hacen falta más salarios para comprar un metro cuadrado, mientras que un aumento del indicador implica que se requieren menos. VER MÁS: Inversión inmobiliaria en Buenos Aires: en qué barrios conviene invertir El informe reveló que el precio promedio de oferta publicado del M2 para el conjunto de barrios históricamente relevados por UADE (Recoleta, Palermo, Belgrano y Núñez) fue de US$3.388. En el caso de los departamentos nuevos el valor fue de US$3.934, mientras que para los departamentos usados el valor fue de US$3.125. Así, los precios de los departamentos nuevos aumentaron 3,2% y los usados cayeron 3,6% en relación con el año anterior. Considerando todos los barrios de la Ciudad, los precios para el segmento “a estrenar” rondaron entre los US$1.691 (Constitución) y los US$5.183 (Puerto Madero), mientras que para el segmento usados los valores oscilaron entre los US$ 1.101 (Villa Lugano) y los US$4.868 (Puerto Madero). VER MÁS: ¿Pozo o usado? Qué conviene hoy para comprar un departamento en Argentina De esta manera, el precio promedio para todos los barrios de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires es de US$2.417, con los departamentos nuevos exhibiendo precio promedio de US$2.831 y los usados de US$2.236. El índice de salario real presenta una caída con respecto al mes anterior para los inmuebles nuevos y usados, debido al aumento del valor del M2 y a la disminución de los salarios en dólares. De junio a julio, el valor del índice cayó de 70,8 a 68,4 para los departamentos nuevos y de 82,4 a 80,0 para los departamentos usados. Pero en términos interanuales, el comportamiento de estas variables implicó que, durante julio, el salario haya podido comprar el 28,6% de un M2 nuevo en la zona norte de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, proporción que es mayor a la registrada en igual mes de 2025, cuando alcanzó al 26,7%. Similar situación se verifica para el caso de las viviendas usadas, para las cuales el ISRV mostró un incremento interanual del 14,8%. En este caso, el salario permitió adquirir el 36,0% de un M2 de vivienda, proporción mayor al 31,3% registrado en julio de 2025. Mirando el largo plazo, el informe también muestra cómo evolucionó la cantidad de salarios necesarios para adquirir un M2 de vivienda en cada mes desde enero de 2010. Allí se observa que la proporción venía mostrando una mejora en los últimos dos años (desde julio de 2024), pero que aún no logró recuperarse de la importante pérdida de poder adquisitivo del salario entre 2019 y 2023. items.title: トランプ氏、習主席との会談を「生産的」と強調－詳細は明かさず
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： トランプ米大統領は、中国の習近平国家主席と「非常に生産的な会談」を行ったと述べた。しかし、会談での合意や進展について具体的な内容は明らかにしなかった。

トランプ氏は25日朝、SNSに投稿し、前日の会談は「米中双方」にとって有益だったとの認識を示したうえで、「今後、素晴らしいことが起きるだろう」と述べた。

ただ、投稿では貿易や輸出規制、台湾問題、AIの覇権争いへの対応など、米中関係を緊張させてきた課題について、具体的な合意や進展は示されなかった。

トランプ氏はAIにも触れたが、人工知能を「スーパーインテリジェンス」と改名しようという自らの主張に重点を置いた。この主張には揶揄（やゆ）する声が上がっているほか、AIが雇用や環境、さらには人類そのものに及ぼす脅威にトランプ氏が向き合っていないとの批判も出ている。

トランプ氏は、習氏もこの改名に賛成したと主張。「あまりいい名前ではなく、しかも実態にも合っていない『人工知能』を、もっと的確で意味のある『スーパーインテリジェンス』と呼ぶことを、彼も気に入ったようだった」と述べた。

今回の習氏のワシントン訪問は、経済・軍事上のライバル国の首脳を、レッドカーペットや軍の音楽隊の演奏、豪華な国賓晩さん会で手厚くもてなすなど、華やかな演出が目立った。ただ、主な懸案への対応では、具体的な成果はほとんどなかった。

唯一の大きな発表は、習氏が米国に到着した23日夜にベッセント財務長官が明らかにした、貿易休戦の延長だった。11月に期限を迎える予定だった休戦を、1月10日まで延長するという内容だ。中国側は延長についてまだ確認していない。

items.title: Italy's Eni caps fuel prices as Meloni struggles to tame rising costs
items.author: Francesca Landini
items.creator: Francesca Landini
items.summary: Italian state-controlled energy group Eni on Friday said it would cap fuel pump prices for at least one month, supporting Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's efforts to curb energy costs.
items.body:
Italian state-controlled energy group Eni (ENI.MI) on Friday said it would cap fuel pump prices for at least one month, supporting Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's efforts to curb energy costs.
Eni said its Enilive unit would sell diesel at no more than €2.19 per litre and petrol at no more than €1.99 per litre, starting from Monday, saying it represented a discount of around 17 cents from current average prices.
"The government thanks Eni for the important initiative," Meloni's office said in a statement, calling it "a commendable gesture of consideration for Italy."
The price cap will be valid for an initial period of 30 days, with the possibility of extending it through the end of the year, depending on market and supply trends, the company said.
Meloni's administration has repeatedly renewed temporary cuts in fuel excise duties in recent months, spending around €2.8 billion, when also including tax breaks for truck drivers.
The latest cut of around 12 cents per litre applies only to diesel and expires on Friday. It is set to be reduced to around 6 cents per litre from September 26 to October 5.
Eni noted that geopolitical crises, combined with a shortage in Europe's refining capacity, had "driven fuel prices to levels that are extremely burdensome for Italian households and businesses."
It presented its price cap decision as "a further gesture of solidarity toward the country, consumers, and its customers," saying it had already refrained from fully passing on cost increases to consumers.
The National Consumers Union also praised Eni's move, while suggesting that it could persuade the government to back off from mooted plans to introduce a windfall tax on energy companies.
Economy Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti has said he would prefer a coordinated move at the EU level but has not ruled out a domestic windfall tax, as the government prepares the 2027 budget law, to be unveiled next month.

items.title: EFL seeks £1 billion from Premier League over five years, Sky reports
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The English Football League has asked for payment of £1 billion ($1.3 billion) over five years from the Premier League amid ongoing negotiations for a new revenue-sharing deal in English football, Sky News reported on Friday.
items.body:
The English Football League has asked for payment of £1 billion ($1.3 billion) over five years from the Premier League amid ongoing negotiations for a new revenue-sharing deal in English football, Sky News reported on Friday.
Premier League clubs were told at a meeting on Thursday that the EFL was seeking annual payments of £207 million over five years, the report added.
Media reports said earlier this year that the Premier League had proposed paying £1.5 billion over 10 years, in addition to existing funding provided by the top flight.
An EFL spokesperson declined to comment on the matter, citing ongoing discussions. Reuters has contacted the Premier League for comment.
Media reports said that the Premier League paid around £137 million to the three lower leagues under the EFL umbrella last season, including the second-tier Championship, League One and League Two.
($1 = 0.7556 pounds)

items.title: Western miners can match China’s speed if African governments cut red tape, KoBold president says
items.author: Maxwell Adombila, Olivia Kumwenda-Mtambo
items.creator: Maxwell Adombila, Olivia Kumwenda-Mtambo
items.summary: The top executive of KoBold Metals said Western miners can match China's pace in developing critical minerals projects in Africa without compromising compliance standards as long as governments streamline approvals and improve coordination among regulators.
items.body:
The top executive of KoBold Metals said Western miners can match China's pace in developing critical minerals projects in Africa without compromising compliance standards as long as governments streamline approvals and improve coordination among regulators.
California-based KoBold, an exploration firm backed by US billionaires Jeff Bezos and Bill Gates, argues that these steps would allow Western investors to deploy capital faster and compete more effectively with Chinese rivals for Africa's critical minerals.
"We reject the assertion that you can't go fast and do things right. You can do both," KoBold President Josh Goldman told Reuters on Monday.
[USN:L8N3Z21F6 TEXT:"Competition for Africa's"] critical minerals is intensifying as the US, Europe and China race to secure supplies of metals vital for electric vehicles, artificial intelligence and defence technologies.
From Democratic Republic of Congo to Guinea, Chinese firms have often outpaced Western rivals through rapid execution, navigating bureaucratic processes and backing mines with railways, ports and processing plants.
KoBold is seeking faster exploration approvals in Namibia while expanding lithium and copper exploration in Congo, Goldman said.
"We would like to accelerate our investment (in Namibia) because we like the rocks, the operating environment, the jurisdiction and the people, but we need to be able to go faster," he said before meeting the country's ministers of international trade and agriculture in New York on Thursday on the company's concerns.
Namibia's Presidency and the ministries of international relations and agriculture did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
KoBold, which has invested about $2 million in Namibia since 2022, holds more than 7,000 square kilometres of exploration licenses there, its largest land position globally by area.
In Congo, KoBold is advancing what Goldman described as the country's largest lithium exploration program, alongside a [USN:L8N40W1T0 TEXT:"major copper exploration"] campaign near the Zambian border as it searches for a world-class discovery comparable to the Manono deposit.
Goldman said the effort was not being slowed by the long-running dispute surrounding Manono, where [USN:L4N3SR01H TEXT:"Australia's AVZ Minerals"] (3A2.H) and Chinese interests remain locked in competing claims.
"Finding the next Manono doesn't depend on what happens with the known deposits," he said.
China's Zijin Mining (601899.SS) began lithium exports from an [USN:L8N43H16J TEXT:"adjoining block at Manono"] in June after building supporting infrastructure, Reuters reported.

items.title: U2 mark 50 years together with concert at school where it all began
items.author: Padraic Halpin
items.creator: Padraic Halpin
items.summary: U2 marked 50 years as a band on Friday by returning to the school where they started playing together as teenagers and delighted current students with a concert featuring hits such as 'With Or Without You', 'One' and 'Beautiful Day'.
items.body:
U2 marked 50 years as a band on Friday by returning to the school where they started playing together as teenagers and delighted current students with a concert featuring hits such as 'With Or Without You', 'One' and 'Beautiful Day'.
The 22-time Grammy-Award-winning band formed in September 1976 after Larry Mullen Jr. pinned a handwritten note reading "Drummer Seeks Musicians To Form Band" on the notice board at Mount Temple Comprehensive School in north Dublin.
Mullen, Bono, The Edge and Adam Clayton on Friday sought to replicate one of their early shows when they played on the roof of the school's boiler room in 1978, the start of a journey that would carve their place in rock history.
Hundreds of students, some holding hand-drawn posters saying "It's A Beautiful Day No School", finished class early and packed the school yard, where they screamed throughout the 35-minute set alongside their similarly enthusiastic teachers.
"Is that the science lab?" said Bono, dressed all in black, as he arrived on stage and pointed to a building in the distance where some teachers watched out of windows and recorded the scene on their phones.
Fans also gathered to listen outside the school gates after word of the secret show spread.
After arriving on stage as Alice Cooper's 'School's Out' blared from the speakers, the band launched into a seven-song set that spanned 'I Will Follow' and 'Out Of Control' from their 1980 debut 'Boy' to 'Vertigo', a UK No. 1 single 24 years later.
Around 30 students from a local music education programme joined on violins, viola and harps for the rendition of 'One'.
U2, whose most renowned albums include 'The Joshua Tree' and 'Achtung Baby', announced this week the release of their 16th album 'Carnaval De Luz' on November 13.
The album, their first in nine years, will feature a duet between Bono and the late Dolly Parton in what the band said was the country singer's last vocal performance. Friday's set also included a live airing of new single 'Silencio'.
Bono thanked the teachers from the "rock 'n' roll high school", some of whom were in the crowd, who helped shape their creativity.
"This island is full of song and music and mischief and we're so proud to be Irish," he said.

items.title: Gucci's Demna blends aristocracy and pop culture at Milan Fashion Week
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Gucci designer Demna on Friday unveiled what he described as his first complete personal vision for the brand, presenting pagoda-shouldered tailoring and cropped, puff-shaped outerwear, as the Kering-owned label seeks to revive growth after a prolonged downturn.
items.body:
Gucci designer Demna on Friday unveiled what he described as his first complete personal vision for the brand, presenting pagoda-shouldered tailoring and cropped, puff-shaped outerwear, as the Kering-owned label seeks to revive growth after a prolonged downturn.
In what Gucci called "The store show", models walked through a series of neutral tone retail-inspired rooms, a setting the brand said offered a glimpse of how Demna's aesthetic could shape Gucci stores in the future.
The show, Demna's third, presented men's and women's collections sequentially.
Former Balenciaga's Demna was appointed Gucci's creative director in March 2025, effective from July, taking over the creative helm of the Kering-owned label after the departure of Sabato De Sarno.
"Gucci moves easily between aristocracy and pop culture, Florence and Hollywood, good taste and bad taste (whatever that means), heritage and mass desire, belonging and rebellion, and the interplay between the two", Demna said.
Sales at Gucci [USN:L6N43U118 TEXT:"fell 3%"] in the second quarter, less than expected, as strong US demand for its new handbags partly offset weaker spending elsewhere, suggesting the group's turnaround efforts may be gaining traction.
Reuters reported this week that Gucci has begun selling new luxury sneaker models [USN:L6N45D0BT TEXT:"labelled "Made in China""], in a break with its Italian manufacturing tradition. Some industry watchers say could undermine the brand's high-end image as it races to win back middle-class shoppers.
Milan Fashion Week, which opened on Tuesday with Prada's show, runs through Sunday. The schedule still includes presentations from Dolce & Gabbana, Bottega Veneta and Giorgio Armani.

items.title: U.S. stocks drift toward the finish of a winning week
items.author: The Associated Press
items.summary: A cooldown in oil prices is clashing on Wall Street with pressure building from the bond market, and the U.S. stock market is making few big moves on Friday.
items.body: NEW YORK — A cooldown in oil prices is clashing on Wall Street with pressure building from the bond market, and the U.S. stock market is making few big moves on Friday. The S&P 500 added 0.3 per cent after flipping between modest gains and losses earlier in the day. It’s coming off a three-day losing streak marred by big swings caused by rising bond yields, but it nevertheless remains near its all-time high set last month and is on track to finish its first winning week in the last three. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 221 points, or 0.4 per cent, as of 11:30 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was 0.3 per cent higher. Stock indexes initially rose after trading began, aided by a drop in oil prices. The most actively traded contract in the market for Brent crude, the international standard, eased 0.6 per cent to US$99.60 per barrel. It’s been yo-yoing on uncertainty about when the war with Iran will allow oil to flow freely again from the Middle East. Prices go down when hopes rise for a possible deal to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz to oil tankers, and they go up when doubts resurface. But a report on U.S. consumer sentiment released shortly after trading began undercut that support because it helped push Treasury yields higher. The report from the University of Michigan said U.S. consumers are bracing for inflation of 4.6 per cent in the coming year, up from their forecast of four per cent the month before. It also said that overall sentiment among consumers was not as bad as economists expected, even if it was the lowest in four months. The expectations for high inflation are potentially dangerous for the economy because they could encourage behavior that leads to a vicious cycle that makes the cost of living spiral even higher. Indeed, some consumers told the survey that buying some kinds of products now would help them avoid higher prices in the future. If they rush to make such purchases, it could encourage sellers to raise prices further. Following the report on consumer sentiment, the yield on the 10-year Treasury rose to 5.20 per cent from 5.18 per cent late Thursday and is near its highest level since 2007. High yields slow the economy by making it more expensive for everyone to borrow money, while undercutting prices for stocks and other investments. Rising yields worldwide are rattling all kinds of financial markets, and yields are climbing not only because of worries about high inflation but also because of big government debt loads, signs of continued economic strength and other factors. The 10-year Treasury yield was at just 3.97 per cent before the beginning of the war with Iran. High yields hit stocks seen as the most expensive in particular. That has pressured stocks in the artificial-intelligence industry that soared in earlier years because of the frenzy around the technology. After the 10-year Treasury yield rose, Nvidia reversed an early gain and dipped 0.1 per cent. A day earlier, its fall of 0.9 per cent was the single heaviest weight on the S&P 500. On the winning side of Wall Street, Akamai Technologies rose seven per cent after the cloud company announced an $11.6 billion, multiyear agreement with Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot. Costco Wholesale added 2.4 per cent after the retailer reported a stronger profit for the latest quarter than analysts expected. Such strong profit reports from U.S. companies have helped the stock market remain resilient despite all the worries about high inflation and oil prices. In stock markets abroad, indexes were mixed in Europe following bigger moves in Asia. Japan’s Nikkei 225 climbed 1.3 per cent, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dropped one per cent. ___ AP Business Writers Chan Ho-him and Michelle Chapman contributed to this report. By Stan Choe

items.title: Florida's Brightline railroad lines up $490 million for bankruptcy restructuring
items.author: Dietrich Knauth
items.creator: Dietrich Knauth
items.summary: Florida's Brightline commuter railroad said Friday that it has lined up $490 million in new financing to restructure some of its parent company debt, while leaving other bond debt untouched.
items.body:
Florida's Brightline commuter railroad said Friday that it has lined up $490 million in new financing to restructure some of its parent company debt, while leaving other bond debt untouched.
17 Brightline affiliates filed for Chapter 11 in New Jersey late Thursday.
Brightline Trains Florida LLC, the train operating company, will remain outside of bankruptcy.
Brightline said the debt restructuring will not impact $2.2 billion in bond debt that was used to finance the company's rail construction.
Brightline operates a high-speed Miami-to-Orlando private rail line.
The debt restructuring will allow the rail company to re-invest in operations and capitalize on "real momentum," Brightline CEO Patrick Goddard said.
Ridership is up 14% from last year and revenue is up 17%, according to Brightline.
Bankruptcy petitions list over $1 billion in assets and over $1 billion in liabilities.

items.title: Huracán Polo vuelve a fortalecerse a medida que se aleja de costa mexicana
items.author: Dante Alfaro
items.creator: Dante Alfaro
items.summary: El huracán Polo volvió a fortalecerse el viernes y alcanzó la categoría 5, la máxima escala en la potencia de vientos, a medida que se iba alejando de la costa occidental de Mexico e internando en el océano Pacífico, dijo el Centro Nacional de Huracanes (NHC, por su sigla en inglés) de Estados Unidos.
items.body:
El huracán Polo volvió a fortalecerse el viernes y alcanzó la categoría 5, la máxima escala en la potencia de vientos, a medida que se iba alejando de la costa occidental de Mexico e internando en el océano Pacífico, dijo el Centro Nacional de Huracanes (NHC, por su sigla en inglés) de Estados Unidos.
A las 8.00 hora local (1400 GMT) Polo se ubicaba a unos 470 kilómetros al suroeste de Cabo Corrientes, un pequeño municipio costero del estado Jalisco, y soplaba vientos máximos sostenidos de 285 kilómetros por hora (km/h), con rachas más fuertes, mientras se desplazaba hacia el oeste a 19 km/h, indicó el NHC. A su paso, dejaba lluvias torrenciales, vientos fuertes y oleaje anómalo.
En la semana, el azote del ciclón obligó a las autoridades a [USN:L6N45G1AV TEXT:"evacuar a decenas de personas"] a refugios temporales, [USN:L6N45F0UV TEXT:"cerrar puertos"] y cancelar clases escolares. En el pequeño poblado costero El Paraíso, en el estado Colima, el mar embravecido arrastró piedras hacia calles cercanas a la playa y provocó daños materiales.
"Tenemos afectaciones por el huracán", reconoció Efrén Pacheco, comisario de El Paraíso, cuya playa se abarrota en verano por turistas que practican diversos deportes acuáticos como surf y windsurf.
"Gracias a Dios, daños a personas no tenemos, pero sí tenemos bastantes daños materiales. Se sienten todavía los efectos del huracán. El mar no le ha bajado, ha estado fuerte", relató mientras se guarecía de una terca lluvia.
Se espera que Polo vire durante el fin de semana hacia el norte y, por primera vez, toque tierra el lunes como un huracán de categoría 2 en la Península de Baja California, cerca del popular destino turístico La Paz. 24 horas más tarde, tocaría tierra por segunda vez cerca de Ciudad Obregón, la segunda ciudad más poblada del estado Sonora.
Aunque se pronostica que Polo perderá algo de intensidad a medida que se acerque y atraviese el noroeste de México, seguirá siendo peligroso, provocando vientos potencialmente dañinos, marejada ciclónica y lluvias torrenciales.
"Polo es un huracán de categoría 5 extremadamente poderoso", advirtió el NHC. "Los residentes de Baja California Sur deben seguir de cerca su trayectoria", agregó.
AccuWeather, una compañía estadounidense que presta servicios comerciales de pronóstico del tiempo, estimó que el ciclón podría provocar inundaciones repentinas y condiciones meteorológicas adversas en el centro-sur de Estados Unidos a finales de la próxima semana, tras amenazar a México como un poderoso huracán con vientos dañinos, lluvias torrenciales y mares peligrosos durante el fin de semana.

items.title: Corte Suprema de EEUU restablece el sistema de verificación masiva de votantes de Trump
items.author: John Kruzel
items.creator: John Kruzel
items.summary: La Corte Suprema de Estados Unidos reactivó el viernes una base de datos sobre inmigración que, según el Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump, tiene como objetivo combatir el voto de personas que no son ciudadanas, pero que los críticos sostienen que podría privar del sufragio a personas con derecho.
items.body:
La Corte Suprema de Estados Unidos reactivó el viernes una base de datos sobre inmigración que, según el Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump, tiene como objetivo combatir el voto de personas que no son ciudadanas, pero que los críticos sostienen que podría privar del sufragio a personas con derecho.
Los magistrados aceptaron la solicitud del Departamento de Justicia de bloquear la orden de un juez que impidió a los funcionarios estatales usar los números de la Seguridad Social y otros datos para hacer comprobaciones exhaustivas de la condición de ciudadanía de los votantes inscritos cotejándola con los registros federales.
El acuerdo de intercambio de datos gubernamental forma parte de una serie de medidas que refuerzan la implicación del Gobierno federal en el proceso electoral antes de los comicios legislativos de noviembre, en los que el Partido Republicano de Trump busca mantener el control del Congreso.
La Constitución otorga a cada estado la autoridad principal para organizar y administrar las elecciones.
El Departamento de Seguridad Nacional rediseñó el año pasado una base de datos federal conocida como "Verificación sistemática de extranjeros para prestaciones» (SAVE, por sus siglas en inglés), usada para verificar la ciudadanía y la situación migratoria de una persona.
Desde entonces, varios estados gobernados por republicanos han cotejado sus listas electorales con la base de datos, y a algunos votantes señalados como posibles no ciudadanos se les ha cancelado su inscripción.
Los críticos dicen que estas medidas de los republicanos no responden tanto a preocupaciones por la seguridad electoral como a un intento de obtener ventaja política reduciendo el electorado, con el riesgo de privar del voto a ciudadanos con derecho a ello que, a menudo, se inclinan por el Partido Demócrata.
Los grupos que presentaron una demanda para bloquear el sistema SAVE revisado afirmaron que el nuevo enfoque ha provocado que personas identificadas erróneamente como no ciudadanos hayan sido eliminadas de las listas electorales.
Argumentan que el sistema SAVE puede estar desactualizado, lo que significa que los inmigrantes que se han naturalizado como ciudadanos estadounidenses y, por lo tanto, tienen derecho a votar, a veces son etiquetados como no ciudadanos.
La tasa de error global del sistema modificado no se conoce públicamente. Ni el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional ni el de Justicia facilitaron la información cuando se les solicitó.
En su escrito presentado ante la Suprema, los grupos de derechos civiles citaron a un funcionario electoral del condado de Travis, en el estado de Texas, quien afirmó que el 25% de las coincidencias de no ciudadanos detectadas por el sistema en esa zona correspondían a personas que ya habían demostrado su ciudadanía estadounidense.
También se refirió a informes periodísticos que revelaron que al menos el 81% de las respuestas del sistema en el condado de San Luis, en el estado de Misuri, eran erróneas.
En una sentencia de junio que bloqueaba la base de datos renovada, la jueza federal de distrito Sparkle Sooknanan, en Washington D. C., señaló que el sistema se elaboró de forma descuidada y contenía datos de ciudadanía poco fiables.
"En definitiva, el Gobierno federal ha pisoteado a sabiendas los derechos de privacidad de los ciudadanos estadounidenses de una manera que amenaza el derecho sagrado al voto", escribió Sooknanan. "Este tribunal no puede quedarse de brazos cruzados mientras eso ocurre".
El Tribunal de Apelación para el Circuito del Distrito de Columbia, en una sentencia de 2 a 1 dictada el 4 de septiembre, se negó a suspender la resolución de Sooknanan, lo que llevó al Gobierno a presentar un recurso ante la Suprema .

Sept 25 : The following is a timeline of Manchester City's Premier League financial rules case, from the charges brought in February 2023 to reports on Friday that the club had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 alleged breaches.
February 6, 2023
The Premier League refers City to an independent commission over more than 100 alleged breaches of finance rules.
City were alleged to have committed multiple financial breaches such as failing to provide accurate financial information, Financial Fair Play breaches, failure to cooperate with investigations, breaching profitability and sustainability regulations and failure to report contracts.

February 10, 2023
City manager Pep Guardiola says the club have already been 'condemned' after being charged by the Premier League.
"It's the same as what happened after UEFA (charges), these are just charges. With UEFA the club proved it was completely innocent. We are lucky we live in a marvellous country where everyone is innocent until proven guilty," Guardiola said.
May 24, 2023
Guardiola says he would like the financial charges against the club to be dealt with "as soon as possible" after City secured a fifth league title in six seasons under the Spaniard.
"Let's go. Don't wait two years. Why don't we do it quicker? In 24 hours, sit down with lawyers present. Let's have it as soon as possible for the benefit of everyone," he said.
June 19, 2023
City Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said the club were frustrated by the situation, saying it detracted from the achievements of the team after they achieved a treble.
"I hope people focus and judge them (the players) for their football, what they're achieving on the pitch and what they're achieving in every competition they're in," he said.
November 15, 2023
City say they earned revenues of 712.8 million pounds ($876.17 million) to June 2023 - an increase of 99.8 million (16.3 per cent) over the previous season, along with a record net profit of 80.4 million pounds.
November 17, 2023
Everton become the first Premier League team to be deducted points for breaching Profitability and Sustainability Rules (PSR) when the league docked the Merseyside club 10 points over their finances in the 2020-21 season.
The Commission determined that Everton's PSR calculation for the relevant period resulted in a loss of 124.5 million pounds - which exceeded the threshold of 105 million pounds permitted under PSRs.
January 15, 2024
Nottingham Forest also face points deductions after being charged by the Premier League for a breach of their PSRs.
January 16, 2024
Premier League CEO Richard Masters tells the Culture, Media and Sport (CMS) Committee of the UK Parliament that a hearing date has been set for City's financial rule breach charges.
"There is a date set for that proceeding. Unfortunately, I can't tell you when that is but it is progressing," Masters said.
February 26, 2024
Everton have their points deduction for breaching Premier League financial rules reduced to six points from 10 on appeal.
March 18, 2024
Forest are plunged into the relegation zone after having four points deducted for breaking financial rules in the 2022-23 season. The club had admitted breaching the threshold of 61 million pounds by 34.5 million.
March 21, 2024
Leicester City also face a points deduction after the Premier League refers the 2015-16 champions to an independent commission over alleged breaches of the league's spending rules.
April 8, 2024
Everton are docked two more points by the Premier League - their second points deduction of the season - after an independent commission found they had breached the league PSRs.
May 7, 2024
Forest are unsuccessful in their appeal to overturn their four-point deduction but the club eventually survives relegation, finishing six points above the drop zone.
May 10, 2024
Everton withdraw their appeal against the two-point deduction after the team secure their top-flight status. They eventually finish 15th in the standings.
September 3, 2024
Leicester City win an appeal against a decision that could have led to a points deduction for an alleged breach of PSRs on the basis that an independent commission ruling on the case did not have jurisdiction.
Leicester's accounting period ended on June 30, 2023, when the club was no longer a member of the Premier League following relegation to the second tier the previous month.
September 16, 2024
Hearing into City's alleged violations of the Premier League's financial regulations begins. Held by an independent commission comprised of three judges, it is estimated to last 10 weeks.
October 7, 2024
In a separate independent hearing, both City and the Premier League claimed victory after an arbitration panel ruled on sponsorship deals, known as Associated Party Transactions (APT), that the club was blocked from completing.
December 6, 2024
Hearing into City's alleged violations concludes, with a decision expected in early 2025.
February 8, 2025
Guardiola said he expected a verdict "in one month", days after City had spent around 190 million pounds on new players in the January transfer window.
August 13, 2025
Ahead of the 2025-26 season, Masters says they have no influence over the decision and cannot speculate on the timings of the case.
"Legal processes rarely take less time than anticipated. We have to be patient," he told Sky Sports.
May 22, 2026
Guardiola announces he will leave City at the end of the 2025-26 season, bringing to a close a decade in charge that delivered one of the most successful eras in English soccer.
June 29, 2026
City appoint former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca as manager from the 2026-27 season, tasking the Italian with building on the success achieved under Guardiola.
August 18, 2026
Masters acknowledged growing frustration over the delay in a verdict on the alleged charges against City, saying the process had taken longer than expected.
September 25, 2026
City were found guilty of all but one of the 115 alleged breaches of the Premier League's financial rules, The Athletic and The Times reported on Friday.
The club are expected to appeal, the reports added.
The Premier League declined to comment. "It's a confidential process, we're not commenting at all," a spokesperson said.
City did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment, but told the BBC that the inquiry into allegations "remains ongoing."
